question: Which of the following is an example of a thermal decomposition reaction?
solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thermal decomposition reaction** is a type of chemical reaction where a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances when heated.
 
• In the given options, **ZnCO3 → ZnO + CO2** (option 3) is an example of a thermal decomposition reaction.
 
• When zinc carbonate (ZnCO3) is heated, it decomposes into zinc oxide (ZnO) and carbon dioxide (CO2).
 
• Other options like the decomposition of water (H2O) and sodium chloride (NaCl) involve different types of reactions such as electrolysis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thermal decomposition** reactions require energy in the form of heat to break chemical bonds in the compound undergoing decomposition.
 
• Common examples of thermal decomposition reactions include the breakdown of calcium carbonate (CaCO3) into calcium oxide (CaO) and carbon dioxide (CO2), and the decomposition of potassium chlorate (KClO3) into potassium chloride (KCl) and oxygen (O2).
 
• These reactions are important in various industrial processes, such as the production of lime from limestone and the preparation of oxygen in laboratories.
